metadata.title: FSI Governance Demo - KYC Customer Portfolio
metadata.purpose: Simulation inputs for AgentCore-powered KYC assessment system

risk_signals: Minority owner is Russian national with frozen assets under EU 10th sanctions package
Company vessels identified in shadow fleet operations transporting Russian crude oil
Ownership restructured 3 weeks after EU sanctions announcement
Ship-to-ship transfers detected in Turkish waters
sanctions_matches: Dmitri Volkov — 92% name match to EU Consolidated List (Council Regulation 269/2014)
Vessel 'MV Petrovsk' flagged in OFAC advisory on Russian oil price cap evasion
adverse_media: Lloyd's List investigation (2023): vessel linked to sanctions evasion network
Norwegian Maritime Authority inquiry into AIS transponder manipulation
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on EU 10th sanctions package (Feb 2023) — EU designated 121 individuals/entities including Dubai-based firms suspected of helping Russia circumvent oil export sanctions. Shadow fleet vessels increasingly used AIS manipulation.
customers.narrative: Norwegian shipping company with a Russian minority owner who appears on the EU sanctions list. Vessels have been linked to shadow fleet operations circumventing the Russian oil price cap. The ownership was hurriedly restructured after sanctions were announced, suggesting awareness of exposure.

customers.enforcement_inspiration: N/A — clean scenario. Representative of low-risk UK agricultural businesses with transparent ownership and regulated operations.
customers.narrative: Well-established British agricultural company with two UK-national beneficial owners, clear corporate structure, and no adverse indicators. Company holds Soil Association certification and publishes annual sustainability reports. Straightforward approval.

risk_signals: Sole beneficial owner previously associated with £365m cash laundering through UK bank accounts
Precious metals sector — high inherent ML risk
UAE free zone incorporation — limited regulatory oversight
Transaction volumes inconsistent with declared business model
Cash-intensive business with deposits at multiple branches
adverse_media: UK Crown Court prosecution (2021): associated entity convicted of money laundering offences
BBC investigation: 'bin bags of cash' deposited across 50 bank branches
Former banking relationship terminated by NatWest following regulatory intervention
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on NatWest £264.8m fine (Dec 2021) — Fowler Oldfield gold dealer deposited £365m through NatWest, including £264m in cash carried in bin bags across 50 branches. First criminal ML conviction of a UK bank under MLR 2007.
customers.narrative: Dubai-based precious metals trader whose sole owner has a history linked to a landmark UK money laundering prosecution. The original scheme involved depositing hundreds of millions in cash at bank branches. Now operating from a UAE free zone with limited oversight — extremely high risk.

customers.enforcement_inspiration: N/A — clean scenario. Represents well-established German Mittelstand tech companies with transparent ownership.
customers.narrative: Mid-sized German enterprise software firm with clear ownership split between two founders and a regulated German VC fund. BaFin-registered fund investor, audited financials, and long operating history. No concerns identified.

beneficial_owners.name: Unnamed BVI holding (Coral Reef Holdings Ltd)

risk_signals: Cryptocurrency exchange — high inherent risk sector
25% ownership through opaque BVI holding company
BVI recently added to FATF grey list (June 2025)
Rapid revenue growth inconsistent with declared customer base
No evidence of robust AML/CTF program implementation
AUSTRAC registration only obtained 8 months after commencing operations
adverse_media: Australian Financial Review (2024): unnamed in AUSTRAC compliance review of crypto exchanges
Reddit threads alleging delayed withdrawal processing and possible commingling of funds
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on Binance $4.3B settlement (Nov 2023) — pled guilty to BSA violations, failure to implement AML program, and IEEPA violations. Also inspired by AUSTRAC actions against Westpac ($1.3B) and Crown Resorts ($450m) for AML/CTF failures.
customers.narrative: Australian crypto exchange with opaque BVI ownership layer and rapid growth. While not directly sanctions-linked, the combination of high-risk sector, jurisdictional opacity, and delayed regulatory registration warrants human review. Could be legitimate rapid growth or could mask illicit flows.

customers.enforcement_inspiration: N/A — clean scenario. Represents publicly listed, FCA-regulated healthcare companies with institutional ownership.
customers.narrative: FTSE 250-listed healthcare group with 25+ years of operating history. Majority institutional ownership, independent board, and Big 4 audited accounts. Transparent corporate governance and regulatory oversight. Clear approval.

risk_signals: Two beneficial owners classified as PEPs (senior government advisors)
Oil & gas sector in resource-rich autocratic state
40% ownership through Cayman Islands fund — UBO unclear
PEP family connections to ruling political party
Source of wealth documentation insufficient
Extractive industry in corruption-prone jurisdiction
adverse_media: OCCRP investigation (2022): 'Azerbaijani Laundromat' — billions moved through UK shell companies
Transparency International: Azerbaijan ranked 154/180 on CPI
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on the 'Azerbaijani Laundromat' (OCCRP investigation) — $2.9 billion laundered through four UK-registered shell companies linked to ruling Azerbaijani elite. Also draws on EU Parliament bribery scandal (2022) involving Azerbaijani political influence.
customers.narrative: Azerbaijani oil company with two PEP beneficial owners and opaque Cayman Islands fund participation. The combination of PEP exposure, extractive industry, and jurisdictional risk requires enhanced due diligence. Not sanctions-listed but governance concerns are significant.

risk_signals: DeFi mixing protocol — facilitates anonymous transactions
Protocol identified in blockchain analytics as processing funds from DPRK-linked Lazarus Group wallets
No KYC/AML controls implemented on protocol users
Smart contracts match architecture of OFAC-designated mixing services
Founder previously employed by entity later added to SDN list
sanctions_matches: Protocol smart contract addresses share 3 common deposit addresses with Tornado Cash (OFAC-designated Aug 2022)
Blockchain analysis: $47m in transactions traced to Lazarus Group-attributed wallets
adverse_media: Chainalysis report (2024): protocol categorized as 'high-risk mixer' facilitating North Korean cyber theft proceeds
Wired investigation: links between development team and sanctioned Blender.io contributors
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on OFAC designation of Tornado Cash (Aug 2022) and Blender.io (May 2022) — both designated for facilitating laundering of proceeds from North Korean Lazarus Group cyberattacks including $620m Axie Infinity hack. Tornado Cash processed $7B+ including $455m for Lazarus Group.
customers.narrative: Delaware-incorporated DeFi protocol whose mixing service has been identified processing funds from North Korean state-sponsored hackers. Architecture mirrors OFAC-designated services. Clear rejection — association with designated entities and proliferation financing.

risk_signals: Baltic bank — jurisdiction historically associated with Russian non-resident banking (Danske Bank Estonia branch scandal)
High proportion of non-resident customer deposits (68%)
Correspondent banking relationships with CIS-country banks
Estonian FSA issued supervisory letter regarding transaction monitoring gaps (2023)
Significant volume of cross-border payments to/from high-risk jurisdictions
adverse_media: Estonian FSA public warning (2023): deficiencies in customer due diligence processes
Financial Times (2024): named in investigative piece on residual Russian money flows through Baltic states
OCCRP 'Laundromat' database: predecessor entity processed suspicious flows 2008-2015
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on Danske Bank Estonia scandal — €200B in suspicious transactions flowed through branch 2007-2015. Also inspired by Deutsche Bank's $186m Fed penalty (July 2023) for insufficient progress remediating AML controls related to Danske Bank correspondent relationship.
customers.narrative: Estonian bank with historical ties to the Russian non-resident banking model that enabled the Danske Bank scandal. Current supervisory concerns and high non-resident deposits suggest ongoing risk. Not sanctioned, but the pattern matches known typologies — requires careful human assessment.

customers.enforcement_inspiration: N/A — clean scenario. Represents established Irish commercial real estate businesses with simple ownership structures.
customers.narrative: Irish property development company with straightforward 50/50 ownership between two Irish nationals. 15+ years of operation, Central Bank of Ireland regulated for relevant activities, clean media profile. No adverse indicators.

risk_signals: Trading in dual-use electronic components (semiconductors, navigation systems)
Export records show shipments to Iran via transshipment points in Malaysia and UAE
Invoice values systematically 40-60% below market price — classic under-invoicing pattern
End-user certificates reference entities in Tehran with no verifiable business presence
South Korean minority owner previously investigated by Korean customs for illegal tech transfers to DPRK
sanctions_matches: End-user 'Pars Electronic Systems' — 87% match to OFAC SDN entity linked to Iranian IRGC procurement
Component types match US Commerce Department Entity List controlled items
adverse_media: South Korean customs investigation (2022): Park Sung-ho questioned regarding dual-use goods transfers
US BIS advisory (2023): Guangdong-based traders named in diversion networks for sanctioned countries
Reuters investigation: electronics supply chains used to circumvent Iran/DPRK sanctions
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on multiple OFAC designations of DPRK/Iran procurement networks (2023-2024) — Treasury targeted networks supplying prohibited components for missile development through Chinese and Malaysian intermediaries. Also inspired by HMRC TBML handbook cases involving over/under-invoicing schemes.
customers.narrative: Chinese trading company shipping dual-use electronics components with evidence of systematic under-invoicing and end-users linked to Iranian military procurement. One owner has prior investigation history for DPRK-related transfers. Classic proliferation financing and trade-based money laundering indicators — clear reject.

risk_signals: Money services business — inherently high-risk sector
Nigerian jurisdiction — previously on FATF grey list (removed 2024)
Rapid transaction volume growth (300% in 18 months)
UK subsidiary bank account receiving high volumes of third-party payments
Correspondent banking relationship terminated by previous bank (de-risking)
Incomplete source of funds documentation for corporate beneficial owner
adverse_media: Nigerian EFCC investigation (2023): sector-wide review of remittance companies — no charges against this entity
De-risking: previous banking relationship with GT Bank UK terminated following FCA enforcement
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on FCA fine of Guaranty Trust Bank UK (£7.6m, Jan 2023) — serious AML weaknesses from 2014-2019 including inadequate enhanced due diligence on high-risk customers and failure to properly monitor transactions. Also reflects broader de-risking of Nigerian MSBs.
customers.narrative: Nigerian remittance business with rapid growth and a previous banking relationship that was terminated. Some red flags present (high volumes, incomplete documentation) but the company may simply be a legitimate high-growth fintech in an underserved corridor. Requires enhanced due diligence and human judgment.

customers.enforcement_inspiration: N/A — clean scenario. Represents well-established Nordic family businesses with long track records and low-risk profiles.
customers.narrative: Second-generation Swedish forestry company with 25+ years of operations. Family trust ownership is fully transparent (Swedish trust registry), FSC-certified operations, and audited by Deloitte. Very low risk — straightforward approval.

risk_signals: Majority state-owned by Belarusian government — subject to EU/UK/US sanctions
Belarus designated under multiple sanctions regimes (EU Council Decision 2012/642)
Minority owner is senior official in Lukashenko administration
Products include dual-use industrial components
Country subject to EU arms embargo and trade restrictions
sanctions_matches: Belarusian State Property Committee — designated entity under EU Belarus sanctions (Council Regulation 765/2006)
Nikolai Karpovich — 94% match to EU designated person (close associate of President Lukashenko)
Entity type matches EU sectoral sanctions on state-owned Belarusian entities
adverse_media: EU Council press release (2022): Belarus sanctions expanded to cover state-owned enterprises supporting regime
Bellingcat investigation: Belarusian state enterprises facilitating Russian military logistics
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on EU sanctions packages against Belarus (2020-2024) — restrictive measures against 233 individuals and 37 entities including state-owned enterprises. Council Regulation 2022/355 expanded measures following Belarus complicity in Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
customers.narrative: Belarusian state-owned industrial manufacturer with majority government ownership and a PEP minority owner linked to the Lukashenko regime. Multiple sanctions matches across EU, UK, and US lists. Automatic rejection — clear sanctions exposure.

risk_signals: PEP beneficial owner — former deputy minister of economy (left office 2021)
Investment fund targets Golden Visa real estate for non-EU nationals
Luxembourg fund structure — while legitimate, adds complexity to UBO identification
Source of wealth for PEP: declared consulting income but significant property holdings
Recent media coverage of Portuguese Golden Visa programme corruption investigations
adverse_media: Público newspaper (2023): Ricardo Ferreira named (not charged) in investigation into Golden Visa programme irregularities
Portuguese MP inquiry (2024): testimony regarding influence of former officials in investment approvals
No criminal charges filed — investigation ongoing
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on Portugal's Golden Visa corruption scandal (Operation Lex, 2023-2024) — multiple government officials investigated for granting residency permits in exchange for bribes. Programme suspended for real estate investment in Oct 2023. Former ministers and judges implicated.
customers.narrative: Portuguese PE fund with a former government minister as beneficial owner, investing in a programme currently under corruption investigation. While not charged, the PEP status combined with adverse media and the nature of the investment programme requires careful escalation for enhanced due diligence.

customers.enforcement_inspiration: N/A — clean scenario. Represents regulated Canadian fintech companies with transparent venture-backed ownership.
customers.narrative: Ontario-registered payment processor with FINTRAC MSB registration. Two Canadian co-founders plus a regulated Canadian VC fund. Clean regulatory history, annual OSFI compliance reviews, and no adverse media. Standard approval.

customers.jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates (Jebel Ali Free Zone)
risk_signals: Nominee ownership structure — true UBO of 60% holding unclear
Free zone entity with limited regulatory oversight
Trade patterns show circular invoicing between related entities in Turkey, Iraq, and UAE
Invoice values for textile shipments 3x above market rates — over-invoicing pattern
Multiple cash deposits in dirham at UAE exchange houses
Company age inconsistent with claimed trading volume
adverse_media: FATF typology report (2023): UAE free zone textile traders identified as TBML conduit
UAE Central Bank circular (2024): enhanced reporting requirements for free zone MSBs
customers.enforcement_inspiration: Based on HMRC TBML Handbook (Operation A) — organized crime group used fabricated trade documentation and over/under-invoicing to launder proceeds through corporate structures that existed only to facilitate money laundering. Also draws on FATF 2023 TBML indicators.
customers.narrative: UAE free zone textile trader with nominee ownership hiding the true beneficial owner. Circular invoicing patterns and systematic over-invoicing strongly suggest trade-based money laundering. The nominee structure prevents proper UBO identification — escalation required for deep-dive investigation.

risk_signals: Wealth management sector carries inherent ML risk — but mitigated by FINMA regulation
Swiss jurisdiction — strong AML framework
customers.enforcement_inspiration: N/A — clean scenario with minor inherent sector risk. Represents FINMA-regulated Swiss wealth managers with long operating history.
customers.narrative: FINMA-licensed Swiss wealth management firm with 18 years of clean operating history. Two Swiss-resident beneficial owners, annual FINMA audits, and membership of Swiss Bankers Association self-regulatory organization. Sector carries inherent risk but strong regulatory environment provides comfort. Approve.
